prospect.name: Luke Charleston
prospect.location: New Jersey, USA (lives a mile from the beach); office in Times Square, New York City
prospect.occupation: Attorney — bills in tenths of an hour, commutes to a Times Square office one to three days a week, roughly three hours round trip by car, ferry and subway
prospect.family_status: Married; wife very active and used to teach spin. Three children aged 14, 12 and 10.
prospect.training_background: Lifelong athlete — ice hockey, baseball, rugby in college, always lifted. Seven or eight years of CrossFit on and off, now transitioned to bodybuilding using the Mayhem Athlete app he pays for personally, plus a CrossFit gym membership. Has also tried THENX bodyweight training, pure powerlifting and yoga. Trains in the mornings, wears a Whoop. Plays golf and winter beer-league ice hockey. Sees a physical therapist for manual work on his back.
prospect.medical: Unrepaired SLAP tear in the left shoulder from an ice hockey injury at 18, never surgically fixed; recurring rotator cuff soreness and restricted shoulder mobility. Herniated disc in the back, ongoing 14 years — it was the original reason he took up CrossFit, to strengthen his core. Currently managing a calf pull. Describes cumulative wear from hockey, rugby and years of lifting: 'my body's just sort of beaten up too much'. Avoids jiu-jitsu specifically out of fear for his back. Reports waking stiff and groggy and 'doing the waddle around the house'.

signals: Self-directed and fully capable — runs his own programming off paid apps (Mayhem Athlete, THENX) and has cycled through powerlifting, bodybuilding, CrossFit and yoga without a coach
Anchored hard to a subscription price: 'I was thinking like being the couple hundred bucks a month'
Bought the substitute in the room — took the $200/month self-paced option the moment it appeared and said 'that's really what I'm looking for'

Divergence from the archetype: he was not skeptical of the method at all, he was enthusiastic about it ('I actually think it's probably perfect for me at this point in my life'). The resistance was purely to the price bracket, not to kettlebells.

goals.text: Lose body fat and get leaner and more cut rather than bigger — back down to 200 lb from 215
Get the cardiovascular conditioning back that bodybuilding lost him, without an hour of zone-two on a bike
Still feel like an athlete at 45
Train in a way that stops beating his body up so he can keep going long term — 'this is a marathon, not a sprint for me'
Efficient, effective sessions that build muscle, cardio and mobility at once, to fit an attorney's schedule
Lead by example for three kids and eventually train his eldest son in the gym
Stop jumping in and out of different programmes and settle on one structure

pains.text: Unrepaired SLAP tear in the left shoulder since age 18, rotator soreness and restricted shoulder mobility
Herniated disc in the back for 14 years; avoids jiu-jitsu entirely for fear of his back
CrossFit now hurts him — 'my body's just sort of beaten up too much'; can no longer sustain five classes a week
Recovery has collapsed with age — dragged himself to the gym and could not do anything
Has cycled through CrossFit, Mayhem Athlete, THENX, powerlifting, bodybuilding and yoga without settling
Bodybuilding is making him bigger when he wants leaner, and has no cardio component
No patience for long steady-state cardio — 'I don't have the attention span to do that'
Attorney billing in tenths of an hour plus a three-hour round-trip commute and three kids
Diet slips through the summer — beach-town social life, IPAs; macro tracking is 'not realistic for me'
Wakes groggy and tight, rarely rested; woke at 3:15am and tossed and turned for hours

objections.raw_quote: I was thinking this was going to be much less expensive than this.
objections.rep_response: Asked what number he had in mind, heard 'a couple hundred bucks a month', then asked a single worth question — 'do you feel like getting to your goals is worth $6,000, or it's not worth $6,000 for you?' No isolation question, no HOW-not-SHOULD reframe, no payment-plan mention and no financial-picture questions. When that one question did not land he abandoned the offer and produced a $200/month alternative.

objections.raw_quote: So I think that, you know, I think that I can pursue other options that will, I think there's other paths for me to pursue rather than just throw, you know, pay $6,000 for this.
objections.rep_response: Did not contest the substitutes at all. Never asked what the other paths were, never contrasted them against the app subscriptions and self-directed programmes he had already told the rep had failed to stick. Went straight to offering the cheaper in-house product.

tiers.label: Primal University — Skool community, monthly, cancel anytime, three-month self-paced progression programme, weekly live session with Trevor, no one-to-one coaching. Produced only after the $6,000 offer was declined.

offer.guarantee_mentioned: "there's a guarantee also on that, that in those six months, you will gain at least eight kilos, which is around 17 pounds of weight, extra weight on your baseline kettlebell moves. If for some reason you wouldn't be able to hit that, he will be working with you until you do for free. But actually we didn't have to use this guarantee. It always works because it's purely science."

evidence: Explicit refusal of the offer: 'I'm not going to pay $6,000 a month for this, so thank you very much, and I will pursue a different path.'
Attempted to end the call twice — 'I don't want to waste any more of your time. I really appreciate your time. I'm sorry this didn't work out.'

Counter-evidence: he did not leave empty-handed. He took the $200/month Primal University link and said 'if this works, I'll sign up today and dive in first thing tomorrow, because I'm really eager to get started on this stuff.' That is a different product at a different price, not the offer, so it does not make this a close.
Counter-evidence: no payment was taken on the call for anything, including the $200 tier — the link was sent and he said he would look at it later.
The refusal was stated in terms of '$6,000 a month', which is not the price. See the mis_selling flag; the true total was never restated.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to review the Primal University Skool link later the same day and possibly subscribe at $200/month. Rep left the door open for the full programme: 'after like three, four months, you feel like, hey, maybe I can go further with that, we're always open.' No follow-up call was booked.

notable.note: The most consequential four minutes in the batch. A $6,000 offer became a $200/month subscription in roughly ninety seconds of price hesitation, with no objection play attempted in between and the rep validating the prospect's own number — 'You mentioned 200 bucks... you're almost on point.' Separately, the prospect twice characterised the price as '$6,000 a month' and walked on that basis, and the rep never corrected him even though the prospect had computed it correctly as '$1,000 a month, effectively' thirty seconds earlier. Worth cross-checking whether the Primal University tier appears in any other rep's calls or whether it is being improvised at the point of loss.

quality.notes: Heavy swapping, and it is worst in exactly the passage that matters most. Through 00:36:13-00:36:50 the pricing exchange is attributed almost entirely to the prospect's label, including the rep's line 'Well, if you want to put it like this. It's a transformation thing' and the rep's question 'What number do you have in mind?', while the prospect's answer 'I was thinking like being the couple hundred bucks a month' carries the rep's label. Roles were reconstructed from content. Similar inversions at 00:00:39-00:00:51 (the ages 43 and 45 are attributed to the wrong speakers) and at 00:08:13-00:08:58 (the boxing story belongs to the rep, not the prospect). The line 'that is $200 per run' at 00:38:38 is almost certainly a mistranscription of 'per month' given the surrounding cancel-anytime framing.
